what: Middleware is code that hooks into every step of an agent's loop: before and after the model call, around each model call and around each tool call. Deep Agents is built from middleware: planning, files, sub-agents, summarization and approvals are each a middleware wrapped around one model loop.
like: Like airport security lanes around a flight: every passenger (each model or tool call) passes the same checks in the same order, and any lane can stop, reroute or fix them.
why: Add retries, limits, PII and approvals without touching the agent's prompt or tools
Each concern lives in one small, testable piece
Change the model's input or output at exactly the right moment

steps.d: before_agent runs once per invocation: load memory, check permissions, set up state.
before_model runs each turn, first middleware to last: trim or summarize history, inject todos, count calls.
wrap_model_call nests like functions (the first middleware is outermost). It can call the model zero, one or many times: retry, fall back to another model, use a cache or swap the model.
after_model runs last middleware to first: check the output, redact PII, or pause for a human with an interrupt.
wrap_tool_call wraps each tool: retry with backoff, cap calls, turn errors into messages the model can read. Then the loop goes back to before_model.
When there are no more tool calls, after_agent runs once in reverse order, for cleanup, saving memory or a final check.

numbers.l: hooks: 4 node-style (before_agent, before_model, after_model, after_agent) and 2 wrap-style (wrap_model_call, wrap_tool_call)
default max_retries in ToolRetryMiddleware (backoff factor 2.0, max delay 60 s)
messages kept by default when SummarizationMiddleware compresses history

choices.d: Node hooks (before_model, after_model...) read and update state at a fixed point. Wrap hooks control the call itself, so retries, fallbacks, caching and short-circuits belong there.
before_* run in list order, after_* in reverse, and wraps nest with the first middleware outermost. Put limits and PII guards outside, retries closest to the model.

Use built-ins for common jobs (Summarization, HumanInTheLoop, ModelCallLimit, ToolCallLimit, ToolRetry, ModelFallback, PII, ContextEditing). Write custom middleware for your domain rules, with its own state fields.
FilesystemMiddleware (required: ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file), SubAgentMiddleware (task tool) and opt-in TodoListMiddleware (write_todos) turn a plain agent into a deep agent.

instead.why: The whole harness picture, not just the hooks

breaks.d: The model keeps calling tools and never stops.
breaks.see: Runs that hit time or cost limits
breaks.fix: ModelCallLimitMiddleware and ToolCallLimitMiddleware with exit_behavior end or error

breaks.d: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware pauses the run, but there is no checkpointer to resume from.
breaks.fix: Always pair interrupt_on with a checkpointer

breaks.d: A retry sits outside a call limit, so each retry counts against the limit, or PII is redacted after it was logged.
breaks.see: Limits hit early, PII in traces
breaks.fix: Order the list on purpose: guards outside, retries inside

say: I treat middleware as the harness: one model loop, and every concern as a hook around it.
Retries, fallbacks and caching go in wrap_model_call; limits, error handling and retries for tools go in wrap_tool_call.
Order matters: before hooks run in order, after hooks in reverse, and wraps nest, so I put guards on the outside.

followups.q: How would you stop a runaway agent?
followups.a: Model and tool call limits per run and per thread, plus a summarization trigger so the context never overflows.

followups.q: How do you add an approval step for risky tools?
followups.a: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware with interrupt_on for those tools and a checkpointer, so the run pauses and resumes with approve, edit or reject.

followups.q: Can middleware change the next step?
followups.a: Yes: a hook can jump_to end, tools or model if it declares can_jump_to.

today: LangChain v1 agents and Deep Agents are both built on this middleware system; Deep Agents ships FilesystemMiddleware and SubAgentMiddleware, and task planning became opt-in in v0.7.

check.q: Which hook should hold a retry with model fallback?
check.why: Wrap hooks control the call itself and can call it again.

check.q: With middleware [m1, m2, m3], which after_model runs first?
check.why: After hooks run in reverse order.

check.q: What must you add for human approval to work?
check.why: The run pauses and must be resumed from a saved state.
